solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Room for preparing all we know, longing to intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ken is the range of one's knowledge, all we know
an itch is a restless longing or craving

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where we get ready everything we know, with some yearning butting in.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN is an old Scots word for the range of one's knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'; 'to intervene' sets the longing inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen is the room of a home where food is prepared and cooked.

clue.text: Seaweed that is being found in Scottish waters?

parts.note: kelp is a large brown seaweed
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A seaweed that grows in the seas around Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seaweed' looks like the definition, but the answer is a creature of Scottish folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A kelpie is a shape-shifting water spirit said to haunt Scottish lochs and rivers.

clue.text: Comparatively thin, metallic bar running through deck

indicators.note: running through means passing inside, so the bar sits within the deck

parts.note: a deck is a level or tier, as of a ship or bus
an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A thin metal rod passing through a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnier describes a sound more thin and metallic in tone, like tin.

clue.text: Who, ditching wife, dated girl? I'm ashamed to hear it

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: to date someone is to meet them romantically
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A confession of a scandal: a married man dumping his wife and seeing another woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A home truth is an unwelcome fact about oneself, one that makes the hearer feel shame.

clue.text: What mustn't be done with two legs elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means raised up, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, so two legs give that pair of letters twice

explanation.surface: A forbidden pose: lifting both legs into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so legs give ON twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-no is something forbidden or unacceptable.

clue.text: Ghastly horse going without its carriage?

indicators.note: going without is read as going outside, so the horse word wraps around the carriage word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab was originally a horse-drawn carriage for hire

explanation.surface: A horse left with no carriage to pull might look grim, or so the question pretends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without' looks like lacking, but here means going outside, so the horse surrounds the carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes something gruesome or deathly, a close synonym for ghastly.

clue.text: Part of Evensong, graduate facing it fearfully

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts

indicators.note: fearfully suggests trembling and shaken, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nervous graduate confronting a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magnificat is the canticle of Mary sung at Evensong in Anglican worship.

clue.text: Victor in trouble, cut deeply

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other word

parts.note: care is worry or trouble
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Victor in a fix who has been badly wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut into something deeply, as wood or stone.

clue.text: Investor number one set up gold reserves, perhaps

parts.note: a bull is an investor who expects prices to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the letters read upward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A leading investor establishes reserves of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion is gold or silver in bulk, such as the bars held as national reserves.

clue.text: Motivate last pair of men before besieging foreign fighters

indicators.note: the last pair of a word means its final two letters
besieging means surrounding, so the word for before goes round the fighters

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
GIs are American soldiers, foreign to a British setter

explanation.surface: Rallying the last two men before they lay siege to foreign troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to give vigour or drive, to motivate.

clue.text: Person running on track's the one I report to

definitions.meaning: read literally, someone who manages a railway line
a ... is one's immediate boss at work

explanation.surface: An office worker whose boss is, apparently, an athlete or a railwayman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: In workplaces, a line manager is the direct supervisor to whom an employee reports; whimsically, a manager of a rail line.

clue.text: Solution for washing all dirty people's backs

indicators.note: backs are the rear ends, so the final letter of each of those three words is taken

explanation.surface: A cleaning product that scrubs the backs of every grubby person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lye is an alkaline liquid, a strong chemical solution used for cleaning and making soap.

clue.text: Island's housing inspector books those behaving stupidly

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the island word encloses the rest

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, plus S from the 's
DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An island where a police inspector keeps books full of fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island's' supplies both the island letter and the S, which are split apart by 'housing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiots are foolish people, those who act without sense.

clue.text: Syndicate with one pound investment maturing

indicators.note: investment is read as being invested, put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a ring is a group of people combining for a shared, often shady, purpose
I is the Roman numeral one
a pen is a pound, an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A financial syndicate putting a single pound into an investment that is slowly growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money but is the animal enclosure, and 'investment' means being placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripening means coming to maturity, as fruit or plans develop over time.

clue.text: Expanse of sand and desert a bonus for sailors?

parts.note: a shore is the land along the edge of the sea
to desert is to leave

explanation.surface: A beach and an empty desert: treats for a weary seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore leave is time ashore granted to sailors, a welcome perk.

clue.text: Kind but uncouth fellows nourish mad dog on the loose

indicators.note: something on the loose is running free and wild, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Good-hearted but crude men who feed a rabid dog that has escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough diamond is a person of good character beneath unrefined manners.

clue.text: Kind son gripped by aversion to speed

parts.note: a make is a kind or brand

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so the son letter goes within the aversion

parts.note: hate is a strong aversion

explanation.surface: A gentle boy who dislikes going fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To make haste is to hurry, to speed along.

clue.text: Conservative faction left in party raised barrier

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other piece
in a down clue raised means turned upward, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
a guard is a protective barrier

explanation.surface: A group of right-wingers, abandoned at a party, put up a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The old guard are the traditionalist members of a group who resist change.

clue.text: Grub favoured by Hell's Angel?

definitions.meaning: the larva of the crane fly

explanation.surface: Food beloved by a motorcycle gang member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food but is an insect larva; Hell's Angels are a notorious motorcycle club.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly larva is called a leatherjacket for its tough skin; the garment is a biker staple.

clue.text: Do away with hollow effect round moulding

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or abolish

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inside, so just the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: Getting rid of an empty effect surrounding some architectural trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the containment signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulet is a small ring-shaped fillet or moulding around a column.

clue.text: Troops engaged in uphill jog suffering

indicators.note: engaged in means placed within, so the troops go inside
in a down clue uphill means reading upward, so the letters reverse

parts.note: to trot is to jog
men are troops, soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers enduring an exhausting uphill run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uphill' turns TROT into TORT, which then holds MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe mental or physical suffering.

clue.text: Extremely cocky, continental journalist passed through revolution?

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A brash European reporter who lived through a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' looks political but means a turning cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to go through a repeating round, a revolution, or to ride a bike with turning wheels.

clue.text: In army officer's wake, I join up with good humour

indicators.note: in someone's wake means following behind them, so the next letters come after the officer

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for General
to ally is to unite or join up with another

explanation.surface: Following a senior officer, I enlist cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Genially means in a friendly, cheerful manner, that is with good humour.

clue.text: Fiction penned by an incomer

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the fiction goes within the other piece

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth

explanation.surface: A novel written by a newcomer to the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or outsider, someone who has come in from elsewhere.

clue.text: Boat that has fortified wine, heading 90 degrees off course

indicators.note: the heading of the word is its first letter, a compass point here, turned a quarter of the way round

parts.note: sherry is a fortified wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A boat carrying sherry that has drifted a right angle from its route.
explanation.walkthrough: S (south) turned 90 degrees on a compass becomes W (west).
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or a barge used on rivers.

clue.text: All that's left of prime steak?

definitions.meaning: a remnant, what remains of a larger body
... steak is a choice cut of beef

explanation.surface: A sad question about the remains of a fine cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is a remainder, as in a rump parliament, and also a cut from the hindquarters.

clue.text: Regular occurrences of racial trouble

indicators.note: regular occurrences means taking letters at even intervals, here every other one

explanation.surface: A grim remark about recurring episodes of racial unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in what ails you.

clue.text: Briefly cavorting in sun at hotspot

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: hell is pictured as the hottest place of all

explanation.surface: Someone frolicking in the sun at a sweltering holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges IN SUN AT into INANUTS; 'hotspot' looks like a resort but is HELL.
explanation.definitionFit: In a nutshell is an idiom meaning summed up concisely.

clue.text: Partially divide ten territories, lessening hostility

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Splitting land into ten regions as a partial peace measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is the easing of tension between nations, especially in the Cold War.

clue.text: Make case to hold note that's repeatedly folded

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the note sits inside the other word

parts.note: to plead is to argue a case in court
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lawyer arguing over a musical note in a document folded many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleated fabric is pressed into a series of folds, so it is folded again and again.
